issue.title: RFC: mining, ipc: allow resizing coinbase reservation on an existing BlockTemplate
issue.body:
### Problem

In the Mining IPC interface, `block_reserved_weight` (minimum 2,000 WU) and `coinbase_output_max_additional_sigops` must be chosen upfront in `Mining.createNewBlock(options)`, and `BlockTemplate.waitNext()` reuses those captured options.

In practice, mining clients often don't want a static upfront guess:
1. Changing coinbase size (#33575): When downstream payout outputs grow or shrink (e.g., Stratum V2 `CoinbaseOutputConstraints` or dynamic pool payouts), the client has to `interruptWait()` and call `createNewBlock()`, locking the mempool and rebuilding the entire template just to free or reclaim a few hundred/thousand WU.
2. Multiple downstream profiles (#33389 / #35675): A proxy serving both solo miners (~930 WU total header + coinbase) and multi-output pool channels (16,000+ WU) cannot share a single `BlockTemplate` stream.
3. 2,000 WU static floor (#31384): `MINIMUM_BLOCK_RESERVED_WEIGHT` (2,000 WU) includes a ~1,000+ WU human-error cushion for `-blockreservedweight` CLI users, which isn't needed when an IPC client knows the exact byte weight of its serialized coinbase.

### Proposal

Add a method on `BlockTemplate` (or support inside `BlockTemplateManager`) that derives a new immutable `BlockTemplate` for a given coinbase weight and sigop budget by dropping enough low-feerate transactions/chunks from the existing template in memory, without re-locking `cs_main` or the mempool:

```capnp
# src/ipc/capnp/mining.capnp (inside interface BlockTemplate)
trim @11 (context :Proxy.Context, options: BlockCreateOptions) -> (result: BlockTemplate);
```

Concretely, this only needs to:
1. Record cluster-chunk boundaries in `CBlockTemplate` during `BlockAssembler::addChunks()` so whole dependent chunks (or standalone transactions) are dropped cleanly without stranding low-fee CPFP parents.
2. Copy the kept `vtx` slice into a new `BlockTemplateImpl` (leaving the original template and any active `waitNext()` / `submitSolution()` calls untouched).
3. Subtract the dropped transaction fees from `CoinbaseTx::block_reward_remaining` and call the existing `BlockWitnessMerkleRoot()` and `CoinbaseMerklePath()` helpers (~0.2 ms, lock-free).

### Alternative proposal
If the requirement that the raw template be submittable before trimming is dropped, you can go one step further: have `createNewBlock` / `BlockTemplateManager` snapshot slightly more than 4,000,000 WU of linearized chunks from the mempool (say 4,050,000 WU, maybe ~15–30 extra chunks in memory) and only materialize the CoinbaseTx + Merkle commitments when the client calls `finalize(exact_coinbase_weight, exact_sigops)`, exchanging enough transactions inside the 4 MWU limit with excess chunks to find the best fit.

This can work in conjuction with the above proposal for backwards compatibility (if needed for such a new interface), where `createNewBlock` can trim it to the requested size.

### Questions for Feedback
1. Does this belong as a method on `BlockTemplate`, transparently inside `BlockTemplateManager` (#35675), or both?
2. Does it make sense to drop the 2,000 WU `MINIMUM_BLOCK_RESERVED_WEIGHT` safety cushion for the IPC path to the actual header + base-coinbase structural weight (~776 WU), letting the client trim the exact additional weight its coinbase needs?

events.body:
This is a duplicate of https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/issues/35596. The main question is: do we want to be pedantic and allow the absolute minimum, which may let users shoot themselves in the foot or assume there is a minor accounting bug having the absolute minimum may causes us to create an invalid block?
Historically, we've been conservative and left a few unused blocks in case of such incidents.  See https://github.com/bitcoin/bitcoin/pull/36156 for related discussion.

Apologies, I missed that issue. It is in the same area, but one noticeable difference with the alternative approach is that the block is sealed (by lack of better name) when the exact sizes are known, so all accounting happens internally. This removes the need to pre-determine the reserved space, and takes the foot-gun out of the users hands. It does add some computation at the `finalize` call, but re-ordering the tail of the block and rehashing a small part of the merkle tree should be really fast.

Shall I close this issue and add a comment there?
